fields.sample_size: three public civil actions on basic sanitation in Aquidauana (Mato Grosso do Sul), Tubarao (Santa Catarina) and Santa Maria (Rio Grande do Sul), followed through court dockets
fields.effect_estimate: Judicial decisions ordering sanitation services (with deadlines, settlements and fines for non-compliance) exist but there is a large gap between judicial recognition of the right to sanitation and its implementation on the ground; court websites carry no information on actual execution of the decisions. The authors argue courts can pressure the executive to prioritise sanitation but cannot alone deliver implementation (technical and financial factors), and call for better judicial databases on execution and for community, media and public-official involvement. Complements Barcellos (2014) quantitative litigation study; qualitative case analysis, no effect estimate.
fields.study_design: doctrinal qualitative case analysis of three public civil actions (docket review)
fields.section: Full text: Case analyses of the three actions (sections on each municipality); Conclusao
fields.exact_location: Case analyses of the three actions (sections on each municipality); Conclusao

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a docket-based analysis of three Brazilian public civil actions on sanitation (Aquidauana, Tubarao, Santa Maria), read in full text 2026-10-04. Courts recognised the right and imposed deadlines and fines, but execution lagged and court websites record nothing on implementation. Three cases, qualitative.
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; names the three actions. Direct evidence on the 'judicial review/sanction' mechanism (implementation gap).
